name: 34. Gemini/Vertex countTokens full-prompt accounting (PR #5620)
description:
Regression: CountTokens unconditionally deleted systemInstruction, generationConfig and toolConfig from the
request body for BOTH Gemini and Vertex, so :countTokens reported only the "contents" token count. Reported
case: a ~7.4k-token system prompt plus a tool declaration counted as 17 tokens on Vertex.

The two endpoints need opposite request shapes, which is why one strip broke both:
  - Gemini (generativelanguage): CountTokensRequest accepts only "contents" and "generateContentRequest".
    systemInstruction/tools/toolConfig/generationConfig are 400 "Unknown name" at the top level and must be
    wrapped in the envelope. Top-level "contents"/"model" are then SILENTLY IGNORED, so the body must carry
    the envelope and nothing beside it. Before the fix, "tools" was never stripped, so any tool-bearing
    countTokens was a hard 400 rather than an undercount.
  - Vertex (aiplatform): CountTokensRequest takes contents/systemInstruction/tools/generationConfig FLAT and
    has no envelope. Only toolConfig (plus safetySettings/cachedContent/serviceTier/labels) is rejected.

The /genai ingress must therefore parse both shapes and emit whichever the resolved provider requires, and
the Bifrost-only "fallbacks" routing field must be honoured for routing yet stripped before the upstream call.

Assertions are relative, not absolute: token counts drift across model versions, so each provider records a
contents-only baseline and every later case asserts the count exceeds it. A dropped field collapses the count
back to the baseline, which is exactly what these cases catch. 400 is deliberately NOT in the infra guard —
for the tools/toolConfig/fallbacks cases a 400 IS the regression signature.
